comparison: Both address the Itô convention choice (C17, C18, C68, C69, C71). OpenEval finds the theoretical description well-established but notes the choice requires stronger justification (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers strongly criticize the choice as insufficiently justified and potentially inappropriate for cellular systems (UNSUPPORTED), with Reviewer 3 stating the authors provide no justification beyond cells being out-of-equilibrium.

Both evaluate the justification for the Itô convention (C71, C72, C73). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN, noting limited justification beyond nonequilibrium nature of cells. Peer reviewers are more critical (UNSUPPORTED), with all three reviewers challenging the adequacy of this justification and questioning whether the convention is appropriate for intracellular environments.

Both address the core diffusive lensing phenomenon (C3, C19-C22, C48). OpenEval finds simulations well-supported but notes biological relevance depends on Itô convention appropriateness (SUPPORTED with caveat). Peer reviewers fundamentally challenge novelty and biological relevance (UNSUPPORTED), with Reviewer 3 calling the probability gradient effect 'trivial' and Reviewer 2 noting it's already been reported.

Both evaluate simulation results showing accumulation (C19, C20, C21, C22). OpenEval finds the simulations technically sound and clearly demonstrate the phenomenon (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers don't dispute the simulation results themselves but question their interpretation and significance (UNCERTAIN), with Reviewer 3 stating the gradient effect is 'trivial once formulated this way.'

Both address biological relevance claims (C4, C5, C6, C50, C51, C77). OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN, noting broad statements not directly supported by simulations and dependence on Itô convention validity. Peer reviewers are more critical (UNSUPPORTED), with all three challenging novelty and biological relevance, and Reviewer 1 concluding 'the relevance of the presented results for biology remain unclear.'

Both evaluate clustering with interactions (C23-C28, C54). OpenEval finds the results supported by simulation data, with reasonable heuristic model (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers are critical (UNCERTAIN), with Reviewer 2 noting it could provide new results but is 'not rigorous enough' and Reviewer 3 criticizing the neighbor-sensing scheme as 'not physically motivated' and violating thermodynamic laws.

Both address MSD analysis findings (C29-C38, C52, C62). OpenEval finds these well-supported by data with adequate sample sizes (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 finding the moment analysis potentially interesting but 'not rigorous enough for a theory paper,' and questioning whether the Itô framework makes results biologically meaningful.

Both address claims about biological significance of findings (C52, C62 overlap with C53). OpenEval supports the MSD conclusions (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers challenge the magnitude and biological relevance (UNCERTAIN), with Reviewer 3 noting that diffusion contrasts 'logarithmically compare to chemical potential ones' and arguing experimental validation is needed.

Both evaluate FRAP simulation findings (C42-C45, C57-C59). OpenEval finds these supported by simulation data with reasonable mechanistic explanation (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not explicitly addressing this finding but noting it depends entirely on the validity of the Itô framework which they fundamentally challenge.

Both address speculative claims (C55, C56, C60, C61, C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative hypotheses lacking direct evidence but representing reasonable future directions. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, arguing these claims are undermined by fundamental challenges to biological relevance of the underlying phenomenon.

Both address highly speculative prebiotic chemistry claims (C75, C76). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are creative but lack supporting evidence and should be distinguished from supported findings. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED as part of broader critique that biological relevance claims are based on incomplete evidence.

Both evaluate methodological choices (C78, C81, C83-C86, C88). OpenEval finds methods internally consistent and adequately described (SUPPORTED), though noting Itô convention remains critical assumption. Peer reviewers strongly criticize methodology (UNSUPPORTED), with Reviewer 3 stating authors use 'agent-based custom simulations with little physical motivation' and that neighbor-sensing violates thermodynamic laws.

Both address 2D to 3D extension claims (C49, C79, C80). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting mathematical argument is correct but direct extension not rigorously demonstrated. Peer reviewers don't explicitly address this but their methodological critique (UNSUPPORTED) of the simulation framework undermines confidence in these extensions.

Both address connections to prior work and future directions (C53, C66, C74 vs C52, C53, C62). OpenEval finds these well-justified based on simulation results (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question whether effects are biologically meaningful (UNCERTAIN), with Reviewer 3 arguing experimental validation is needed to prove relevance.

OpenEval finds claims about heterogeneous diffusivity in cells (C1, C7, C8, C46) well-supported by prior literature (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers don't challenge the existence of heterogeneous diffusivity but rather the interpretation of its consequences.

OpenEval finds knowledge gap characterization (C2, C13, C16, C47) reasonable and justified (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers challenge whether the study actually addresses a genuine gap, with Reviewer 2 noting the phenomenon 'is not new.'

OpenEval finds literature citations and context establishment (C9, C10, C11, C12, C14, C15, C63-C65) appropriate and accurate (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers don't challenge the background literature but rather the novelty and interpretation of the current work.
